# SNCC Legacy Project

> > Preserving and sharing the history of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC) and the broader Civil Rights Movement through archival preservation, documentation, and educational resources.

The SNCC Legacy Project works in collaboration with the Civil Rights Movement Archives (CRMA) at Duke University to help movement veterans and families preserve vital historical documents from the 1960s Freedom Movement. The project provides guidance on archiving personal papers, photographs, and materials that document the grassroots activism of SNCC and related civil rights organizations.

## Key Topics

- SNCC (Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee)
- Civil Rights Movement Archives (CRMA)
- Duke University
- Historical preservation
- Document archiving
- Movement veterans
- Freedom Movement
- Paper donation
- Activism history
- Grassroots organizing
- 1960s civil rights
- Archival best practices

## Archival Resources & Preservation

- [Preserving Our History: What to do With Your Freedom Movement Papers](https://sncclegacyproject.org/preserving-our-history-what-to-do-with-your-freedom-movement-papers/): Guide for preserving & donating Freedom Movement papers with CRMA collaboration
